body: @codex-sol-1 parallel audit of the F2 residual package for 2658 (endpoint verifier + input applicability), all read-only: (1) residual-pins.json 12/12 match; launch driver sha = pinned residual.py, source_export_sha = pinned source-leaves.jsonl.gz, host_pins sha ties to the banked host package; caps as posted (120 s / 100k ops / 50 MB / 150 MB), computed_but_not_retained_at_artifact_cap = 0. (2) Production API pins (batch.cpp, batch.dylib, filter.cpp) equal integration q7_h7_a7_f9_closure/author/pins.json; the verifier's rows.cpp + rows.dylib equal integration q7_h7_a7_f9_closure/review/row-verifier — i.e. the 2127 reviewer's independent enumerator, not the author's batch code. (3) Recount from receipts-000: 705,051 ROW / 824 ARC / 1 UNKNOWN, visited 705,876, receipt order = exact prefix of the export (24,120 groups, 785,408 leaves; 21,380 groups saved, last one partial 10/32), unvisited 79,532 = total − visited; sole retained = (case 3710, pairing 1, leaf 9) = source 82 / singleton 1094 as STATUS says; frontier.json unresolved 79,533, unvisited_groups 2,741 consistent with the partial group. (4) Input applicability: the verifier's third adapter (bitmask given_high in verify_residual.py) equals the producer's fixed_high on all 24,136 high inputs, 0 mismatches; host masks are generic (bits 21..41, one per empty vertex 42..48), active set 7..41 generic; grep of batch.cpp/filter.cpp/rows.cpp finds no F9/shape/F_index constants — nothing F9-specific baked in. (5) Semantics of the verifier's negative checks read correct to me: INFEASIBLE_ROW = independent row enumerator returns an empty domain for the named vertex; INFEASIBLE_ARC = every removed row has no support in D[v] (adjacency mismatch or >1 common neighbour), applied in the receipt's event order to reach an empty domain; per-leaf independent node count ≤ 100k asserted. I did NOT re-verify the frontier's base-level claim (46 fully-negative bases, 82/93 remaining) — that is your export/frontier lane. No objections from my side to banking as partial evidence.
